_comment: Allow rules must live here rather than in settings.json: a project settings.json's allow rules are ignored until the workspace is trusted, and under `--permission-mode dontAsk` that denies every call, so a scheduled run fails having written nothing - the same way every time, quietly. Local settings need no trust.
_comment_noshell: There is deliberately NO Bash or PowerShell allow rule. This bot's agent reads JSON and writes prose; every network read and every mail operation is done by scripts/collect.py and scripts/triage.py, invoked by run_sweep.ps1 before and after the agent runs. That is the same split finance-research uses for its broker, and it is what makes the trash bin auditable: the model explains the classification, it never performs one. If the agent could shell out, it could also reach imaplib directly, and then no rule in classify.py would be load-bearing any more.
_comment_nofetch: There is also no WebFetch and no WebSearch. This bot summarises what arrived; it has no reason to go and read the internet, and a bot holding live mail credentials is the last one that should be following links out of the messages it just read.
_comment_env: Read(./**) deliberately does NOT include .env or state/graph-token.json - both are carved back out by deny rules in settings.json, which beat these. The agent never needs a credential to write a digest, and a credential in a transcript is a credential in a log file.
